title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
section: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text:
Stochastic PDE solvers have emerged as a powerful alternative to traditional discretization-based methods for solving partial differential equations (PDEs), especially in geometry processing and graphics. While off-centered estimators enhance sample reuse in WoS-type Monte Carlo solvers, they introduce correlation artifacts and bias when Green's functions are approximated. In this paper, we propose a statistically weighted off-centered WoS-type estimator that leverages local similarity filtering to selectively combine samples across neighboring evaluation points. Our method balances bias and variance through a principled weighting strategy that suppresses unreliable estimators. We demonstrate our approach's effectiveness on various PDEs—including screened Poisson equations—and boundary conditions, achieving consistent improvements over existing solvers such as vanilla

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text: In recent years, Monte Carlo partial differential equation (PDE) solvers have significantly influenced the field of computer graphics. These solvers have been applied in various areas, including geometry processing [Sawhney and Crane 2020], fluid simulation [Rioux-Lavoie et al . 2022; Sugimoto et al . 2024], and cage-based deformation [de Goes and Desbrun 2024]. Unlike traditional PDE solvers based on the Finite Element Method (FEM), stochastic PDE solvers eliminate the need for spatial discretization and offer an efficient methodology for solving boundary value problems. Several stochastic PDE solvers have been developed to address different

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text:
types of PDEs, such as the Laplace, Poisson, and screened Poisson equations, under various boundary conditions, including Dirichlet [Sawhney and Crane 2020], Neumann [Sawhney et al . 2023], and Robin [Miller et al . 2024b]. Sawhney et al . [2022] further extended these solvers to handle spatially varying coefficients. More recently, differentiable stochastic PDE solvers have been introduced to address inverse problems [Miller et al . 2024a; Yilmazer et al . 2024; Yu et al. 2024].
In the WoS-type Monte Carlo solver proposed by Sawhney and Crane [2020], estimations at each evaluation point are independent. Variance reduction methods such as control variates and importance sampling are employed to accelerate the convergence of pointwise estimators. To further enhance convergence by leveraging the underlying PDE structure, recent works [Bakbouk and Peers 2023; Czekanski et al . 2024; Miller et al . 2023; Qi et al . 2022] have introduced correlations between evaluation points using various strategies, achieving remarkable variance reduction.

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text:
An interesting acceleration approach is the off-centered estimator, which has been studied in some cases. Hwang et al. [2015]; Yu et al . [2024] use the off-centered estimator to accelerate the random walk from evaluation points near the domain boundary. For Laplace equations, Czekanski et al . [2024] used the off-centered estimator to introduce correlation between evaluation points and used a deterministic bound to weight the off-centered estimators.
However, when adapting the approach of Czekanski et al . [2024] to a more general setup, we found that the simple off-centered estimator has the following two issues:
- Correlation artifacts. If one reused sample has a relatively large error, it can affect all evaluation points that depend on it, introducing large errors and artifacts.
- Bias: If the off-centered Green's function cannot be computed efficiently and must be approximated, additional bias may be introduced.

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text:
To mitigate these issues, we adopt a statistical weighting scheme inspired by recent Monte Carlo denoising techniques [Sakai et al . 2024], allowing us to suppress extreme points and providing a biasvariance trade-off when using approximated Green's functions.
Our main contributions are as follows.
- An efficient off-centered WoS-type estimator that aggregates information across multiple integration domains using a principled, statistically-weighted combination.
- Extension of the off-centered estimator to a wide class of PDE problems, including those with screened Poisson equations, mixed Dirichlet–Neumann boundary conditions, and gradient field estimation.
- A comprehensive experimental evaluation showing that our method consistently achieves lower variance and error compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

The theoretical foundation of stochastic PDE solvers stems from potential theory and probability. Stochastic PDE solvers can be applied to a wide range of scenarios; for clarity of exposition, we briefly introduce the simplest Laplace equation case. Kakutani [1944]
established the key result:
<!-- formula-not-decoded -->
where 𝑋 is the Brownian motion starting from 𝑋 (0) = 𝑥 and 𝜏 = inf {𝑡 : 𝑋 (𝑡) ∈ 𝜕Ω} is the first-hit time to boundary.
This formulation offers a stochastic approach to solving linear elliptic PDEs: at each point inside the domain, Brownian random walks are simulated, and the solution is estimated by averaging the boundary values at the hitting points. However, explicit simulation is computationally expensive due to the need for small time steps and frequent boundary checks in the temporal difference.

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text:
To address this bottleneck, Muller [1956] proposed the Walk on Spheres (WoS) algorithm, which implicitly simulates Brownian motion. At each step of the WoS algorithm, the distance 𝑑 between the current position 𝑝 and the given boundary 𝜕Ω is computed. The next position is then uniformly sampled on the sphere 𝐵(𝑝, 𝑑). If the distance to the boundary is less than 𝜖, the current position is projected onto the boundary to obtain the sampled boundary value.
The WoS algorithm can also be understood through the mean value property of harmonic functions:
<!-- formula-not-decoded -->
This recursive integration resembles the structure of the rendering equation in physically based rendering [Kajiya 1986], and can be solved via single-sample Monte Carlo estimation.

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text: Sawhney and Crane [2020] pioneered the application of WoS in geometry processing. PDEs are ubiquitous in this field, and traditional approaches often require extensive preprocessing and watertight meshes. Stochastic PDE solvers offer an alternative without discretization requirements. Subsequent works expanded this framework: Sawhney et al . [2022] addressed spatially varying coefficients, Sawhney et al . [2023] developed the Walk on Star method for Neumann boundary conditions, and Miller et al . [2024b] generalized the walk on star algorithm to handle Robin conditions. Differentiable solvers for inverse problems were explored by Miller et al . [2024a]; Yu et al . [2024] and Yilmazer et al . [2024]. Besides the WoS-type Monte Carlo solvers, Sugimoto et al . [2023] introduced the walkon-boundary method, providing an alternative for Monte Carlo geometry processing.

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text: Beyond extending solver applicability, another major focus is accelerating convergence through variance reduction. Sawhney and Crane [2020] employed importance sampling of Green's functions and control variates to reduce variance in the WoS algorithm. Boundary value caching [Miller et al . 2023] leveraged boundary integration to estimate solutions at evaluation points using cached samples from the boundary and domain. Mean value caching [Bakbouk and Peers 2023] sampled domain points and evaluated solutions by utilizing the volumetric mean value property within the maximal sphere of each evaluation point. Reverse WoS [Qi et al . 2022] proposed a bidirectional formulation, emitting random walking particles from both evaluation points and boundaries. More recently, Huang et al . [2025] adapted path-guiding methods from rendering to stochastic PDE solvers, significantly improving cases with sparse source terms.

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text: Neural methods have also been explored: Li et al . [2023] developed neural networks for caching estimation results, while Li et al . [2024] employed neural networks to automate control variate selection. The works most related to our approach are Hwang et al . [2015] and Czekanski et al . [2024]. Hwang et al . [2015] used the off-center formulation to accelerate the random walk. Czekanski et al . [2024] leveraged the Poisson kernel to reuse samples from neighbors, but only Laplace equations are handled.

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text: Despite these advances, challenges remain. For instance, 3D diffusion problems with spatially varying source terms introduce high variance in stochastic PDE solvers. As shown in Figure 1, the mean value caching method generates some correlation artifacts, especially at the positions close to the boundary. Even with the nonuniform sample used by Bakbouk and Peers [2023], some evaluation points close to the boundary can not get enough samples and lead to large errors. Benefiting from the global formulation, boundary value caching [Miller et al . 2023] greatly reduces variance compared with Sawhney and Crane [2020]. But with very few samples and relatively short running time, boundary value caching generates results with relatively large errors.

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text: Monte Carlo rendering has been developed over decades, and many sample reuse strategies were proposed, such as virtual point lights [Dachsbacher et al . 2014; Keller 1997], photon mapping [Jensen 1996], and ReSTIR [Bitterli et al . 2020; Lin et al . 2022; Ouyang et al . 2021]. Many previous variance reduction techniques in stochastic PDE solvers draw inspiration from rendering. For example, Qi et al . [2022] adapted bidirectional path tracing to WoS, while boundary value caching [Miller et al . 2023], inspired by virtual point lighting, employed boundary integration to cache values and derivatives for internal points.

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text: The off-centered estimator shares some similarity with the rendering techniques, such as multiple importance sampling (MIS) [Veach and Guibas 1995] and spatial sample reuse [Bitterli et al . 2020]. To estimate an integral, MIS uses more than one distribution for importance sampling, and the off-centered estimator uses multiple integrals in different domains to estimate the value. The spatial part in ReSTIR [Bitterli et al . 2020] reuses samples from neighboring pixels, and the off-centered estimator also reuses the data from neighboring evaluation points.

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text:
In this section, we describe our choice of weighting coefficients in estimator 8. We adopt a filter-based denoising technique to determine proper coefficients, addressing the following two issues:
- The off-centered estimator introduces correlations between evaluation points. A single outlier with large error can contaminate multiple evaluations that reuse it, causing both visual artifacts and numerical errors (see Figure 3).
- When Green's function is approximated, off-centered estimators are biased. To mitigate this, we must identify low-quality estimators and apply a bias-variance strategy (see Figure 8).

(a): off-centered estimator with the uniform weighting, extreme values affect all evaluation points that reuse them. Artifacts caused by outliers are marked by purple boxes (b): Our statistical weighting strategy can significantly reduce these artifacts.

Intuitively, this approach treats the center estimator 𝐼𝑥 𝐼𝑥,𝑥 as a reference for similarity evaluation. If an off-centered estimator 𝐼𝑥 𝐼𝑥,𝑦 is sufficiently similar to 𝐼𝑥 𝐼𝑥,𝑥 , it is incorporated into the computation. Conversely, if a sample from 𝑦 results in an outlier, it is excluded from reuse in neighboring evaluations, thereby reducing the impact of estimators with large error. As shown in Figure 3, using this sampling strategy can remarkably reduce the correlation artifacts in the off-centered estimator. In Figure 3 (b), there are many noisy points, indicating that outlier estimation happens. Proposed weighting strategy prevents other evaluation points from reusing the extreme data and hence reduces the artifact in Figure 3 (a).
With statistical weighting, the estimator in equation 8 is no longer unbiased even with all 𝐼𝑥 𝐼𝑥,𝑦 unbiased due to the weights depending on the estimates themselves (we do not consider the bias brought by 𝜖-shell for convenience). text: When the variance of the center estimate 𝐼𝑥 𝐼𝑥,𝑥 is high, the method allows some biased off-centered estimators to be included to reduce overall variance. As more samples are collected, the variance of the center estimator decreases linearly, and those biased estimators are gradually excluded. Hence, the described weighting strategy can filter out the highly biased estimators 𝐼𝑥 𝐼𝑥,𝑦 , and we can tune 𝛾 to make a bias–variance trade-off.

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting

text:
In this section, we show our results on solving a variety of 3D boundary value problems and compare the proposed method with vanilla WoS solver [Sawhney and Crane 2020], mean value caching [Bakbouk and Peers 2023], and boundary value caching [Miller et al . 2023].
We implemented the proposed algorithm in C++ and listed pseudo code in algorithm 1. Geometric primitives are powered by the FCPW library [Sawhney 2021]. Experiments were run on a PC with an Intel i5-12500 processor, 32 GB RAM, and only CPU parallelization. For the mean value caching algorithm, we use the non-uniform variant with parameters used by Bakbouk and Peers [2023] since we found in practice that the evaluation points near the boundary commonly have larger error. When there are no samples in the maximal ball of some evaluation point, we add a sample at the center and estimate it with the standard WoS or WoSt algorithm.

text: In this part, we study the effect of different weighting strategies and implementation details in section 4. Firstly, we present results in a simple 2D domain. As shown in Figure 6 (a), for the simplest Laplace equation, the specially designed Poisson bound weight [Czekanski et al . 2024] presented better results than uniform weight and the proposed method. However, for the Poisson equation, the Poisson kernel does not provide a valid variance bound and hence underperforms compared to the proposed method and even uniform weight. We also present the MSE curves (Figure 7) of 3D equations with the boundary defined by model 1 in Figure 5. For the 3D Poisson equation, the proposed method has a slight MSE improvement, but Poisson-bound weighting increased the error since it cannot effectively estimate the variance of estimators. For the screened Poisson equation, the proposed weighting strategy filtered those highly-biased estimators, successfully reducing the bias brought by the approximated Green's function.

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text:
Limitations. We introduced a new statistical filtering method to WoS-type solvers, solving the correlation artifact and bias issues in combining off-centered estimators. While handling these problems, our method has some known limitations. As stated in section 3.2 , our method is no longer unbiased. In the early sampling stage, since the estimates are noisy, our results may generate worse results. It is also worth mentioning that, compared with standard solvers, the off-centered scheme does not keep the mean value property. For simple Laplace equations, the final result may be larger/smaller than the boundary maxima/minima.
Adaptive Strategies. In our current implementation, the hyperparameters in the weighting strategy and the neighbor selection strategy are all fixed. The number of walks from each evaluation point is equal. Making these hyperparameters adaptive is an important future direction.
Denoising. Similar to the development of Monte Carlo rendering, denoising techniques can also be used with stochastic PDE solvers. Although we can directly use the image denoisers used in Monte Carlo rendering, a denoising method specialized for the PDE solvers has not been thoroughly explored.

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text: Pointwise estimators. Our method is compatible with various pointwise estimators. While traditional walk-on-spheres (WoS) algorithms [Sawhney and Crane 2020; Sawhney et al . 2023] employ specific estimators at each step, alternative schemes such as the walkon-boundary (WoB) algorithm [Sugimoto et al . 2023] can also be integrated. Furthermore, enhancements like those proposed by Huang et al. [2025] are orthogonal to our approach and can be seamlessly integrated within the same estimator reuse mechanism.

title: Off-Centered WoS-Type Solvers with Statistical Weighting
text:
We have presented a novel statistically-weighted off-centered estimator for WoS-type PDE solvers in computer graphics. By integrating a similarity-based weighting scheme, our method reduces correlation artifacts and allows for controlled bias when approximate Green's functions are used. This framework generalizes existing off-centered approaches and extends their applicability to a broader class of PDEs and boundary conditions, including the screened Poisson equation and gradient field estimation.
Our experiments show that the proposed method achieves significant variance reduction compared to both standard WoS-type PDE solvers and prior correlation-based techniques. The resulting solver demonstrates robust convergence properties across a wide range of scenarios, offering an effective and general-purpose tool for solving PDEs in graphics applications.
